title: Real-SWAP storage-response and bottom-exchange decomposition

authority.fixture: unchanged F-GC45 physical setup and FMR serialized Reference Richards backend

measurements: accepted storage change in cm and m for each fixed-head whole-window trial
accepted total in, total out and mass residual
accepted bottom outward exchange in cm and m
central finite-difference d(storage_change_m)/dH at the two MAP02 radii
central finite-difference d(bottom_outward_exchange_m)/dH at the same radii
ratio of storage derivative to production u
ratio of bottom-exchange derivative to -production u
hypotheses: d(storage_change_m)/dH is approximately +u within the local admitted band
d(storage_change_m + bottom_outward_exchange_m)/dH is approximately zero because all other active external forcing is head-independent in this fixture
gates: all direct corrector trials are accepted and mass-complete
accepted_storage_change equals accepted_total_in-accepted_total_out within the transaction mass tolerance
all fixed-head mass residuals are finite and within 1e-12 cm
both storage and bottom-exchange finite-difference derivatives are finite
storage derivative and minus bottom-exchange derivative agree within 5e-4 relative
storage derivative agrees with production u within 5e-4 relative
the derivative of storage plus bottom-outward exchange is no more than 5e-4 times the production-u scale
interpretation_rules: If the hypotheses close, u is locally a storage sensitivity dS/dH for this simple fixture, while q_swap has derivative -u/dt.
That result does not imply q_u itself equals physical bottom exchange.
Any conclusion about the application-service reanchor must distinguish a storage/balance response from the corrector bottom-interface flux.
forbidden: do not generalize the storage identity to active drains/root uptake until separately tested
